name: Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder
summary: AI blog builder for Shopify: generates SEO-oriented posts with titles, images and keyword suggestions, embeds your products, and schedules bulk publishing from a drag-and-drop editor. The Shopify listing published no plan block and no credit allowance when we re-read it on 19 September 2026; its pricing field reads Free.
best_for: Shopify stores that want structured, product-linked blog drafts and a publishing schedule, and that will edit what comes out before it goes live
skip_if: you intend to bulk-publish AI articles unedited, or you need to know what a tool costs before you install it, as of 19 September 2026 this listing publishes no plan block and no credit allowance at all
honest_knock:
Publishing volume is the trap this tool makes cheap. It generates posts quickly and schedules them daily or weekly in bulk, and a Shopify blog filled with unedited AI articles is precisely the pattern search engines have spent the last two years demoting: the app lowers the cost of production, not the bar for ranking. Used the other way round, as a drafting and structuring tool for posts you actually edit, it is sensible.

The price is the second thing to watch, and on 19 September 2026 there is none to read. The listing publishes no plan block and gives its pricing as Free. That is not the same as free being the whole story: the features it advertises (AI generation, bulk creation, translation, scheduling) were metered in credits until August, and no credit allowance or overage rate is stated anywhere on the page now. The same developer's other listing still prints a complete ladder, so this one is not simply a developer who does not publish prices. Go in expecting to ask what the limits are, and do not plan a content calendar around an allowance nobody has told you the size of.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/tapita-ai-seo-blog-builder and in our own test that day; earlier: re-read 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/tapita-ai-seo-blog-builder, and again on 2026-10-15 with the same result: no plan block, the header Price field reads Free, and the only dollar figure on the page, $39 a month, belongs to another app in the “More apps like this” rail) The paid tier has left the listing. Where the page carried a Pro plan in August, it now publishes no plan block at all: the Pricing field in the header reads simply “Free”, the word Pricing appears exactly once on the whole page, and the only dollar figure anywhere on it belongs to a different app in the “More apps like this” rail. We checked that against the same developer's other listing in the same session — apps.shopify.com/google-seo-schema-meta-data renders its header as “Free plan available” and prints its full ladder — so this is the state of this listing rather than a page that failed to load. What that removes is everything a buyer could previously plan against: Pro at $9.99 a month on Shopify Basic rising to $14.99, $39.99 and $69.99 by Shopify plan, the $101.89 annual rate, the 250 monthly AI credits and the $0.06 charge for each credit beyond them. The free tier's own allowance is gone from the page too — the 50 non-recurring credits are no longer stated — so as the listing stands there is no published number for what the app gives you or what exceeding it costs. On 19 September the listing was titled Tapita SEO AI Blog Builder and stood at 4.9 from 485 reviews, up from 450 in August. Read on 15 October 2026 it has been renamed Tapita GEO Studio & AI Blog and now pitches being cited by ChatGPT and Gemini alongside ranking in Google. It still carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge, works with Shopify Admin and the developer's own Tapita SEO Optimizer & Speed, is offered in English only, and stands at 4.9 from 488 reviews, distributed 469 five-star, 13 four-star, 2 three-star, 1 two-star and 3 one-star. Read again on 17 November 2026: the listing is now titled Tapita AEO/GEO AI Blog (Tapita SEO AI Blog Builder in August and September, Tapita GEO Studio & AI Blog on 15 October), still has no plan block and gives its pricing as Free, and shows 4.9 from 494 reviews. In our own test the same day on a Shopify development store the app started on a free level with no plan screen and no payment step, labelled Free on its dashboard, with GEO Studio described as free. Its Create blog post form showed “55 AI credits”, the dashboard read “Published posts 0 / 1”, and a banner said that AI writing runs on credits from the developer's separate paid app SEO & Speed, with 50% off its first 3 months until 4 December. That banner is a temporary promotion for another app and not a price for this one. A first draft article took about 45 seconds; setting a publish date was marked as a paid feature. We saw no text confirming the limit of 1 published post, and we did not publish the draft.

claims.observed: The App Store listing is now titled Tapita AEO/GEO AI Blog, the dossier name is Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder; in the Shopify admin the app is called Tapita GEO & AI Blog and its welcome page says Tapita AI Blog Builder. It is one product under three names.
claims.plan: Free level only; no plan screen came up and the paid app SEO & Speed was not opened
claims.comparability: The dossier name against the listing title, the admin name and the welcome page; the name change is a fact about the listing, not a test result.
claims.buying_consequence: The product the dossier calls Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder is now listed as Tapita AEO/GEO AI Blog; the review should say so.

claims.claim: Free per the Shopify listing, with no credit allowance published
claims.observed: The listing price is Free, as in the dossier. In our test (17 Nov 2026) the create form showed 55 AI credits, the dashboard showed Published posts 0 / 1, and a banner said GEO Studio is free while AI writing runs on credits from the paid app SEO & Speed. The button for a visibility date was marked as a locked feature.
claims.plan: Free level only; no plan screen came up and the paid app SEO & Speed was not opened
claims.comparability: The dossier wording against the credit balance, the counter and the banner in the app; no text confirmed the limit of one post and nothing was published.
claims.buying_consequence: Free is true for the install, but in our test (17 Nov 2026) the app showed a credit balance and a counter of one published post, and more writing points to a paid app; the free level may stop after one post.

claims.observed: In our test (17 Nov 2026) the dashboard tile said Published posts 0 / 1 with 1 posts scheduled, which suggests that the free level allows one published post. No text said so and the draft was not published.
claims.plan: Free level only; no plan screen came up and the paid app SEO & Speed was not opened
claims.comparability: The counter on the dashboard against a publish action that was left out on purpose; no limit text was read.
claims.buying_consequence: Whether the free level really stops at one published post is not confirmed.

claims.observed: After 6 clicks plus typing and Generate at about 23:13 the app showed four progress steps and this message after about 45 seconds. The result was a draft with Visibility Hidden; nothing appeared in Shopify Blog posts and Publish was not clicked.
claims.plan: Free level only; no plan screen came up and the paid app SEO & Speed was not opened
claims.comparability: The message in the app against one generation for one keyword; other topics, longer posts and Bulk Generate were not tried.
claims.buying_consequence: A full draft can exist in under a minute from a keyword and a title, on the free level and without a card, but it stays inside the app until you publish it.

claims.observed: The option was switched on in the create form and the draft held an FAQ accordion with questions and short answers. The generated structured data on a published page was not inspected, because the draft was not published.
claims.plan: Free level only; no plan screen came up and the paid app SEO & Speed was not opened
claims.comparability: The option and the FAQ block in the editor against a page source that does not exist yet; no validator was run.
claims.buying_consequence: Whether the FAQ becomes valid FAQPage markup on the live page is not confirmed.

claims.observed: The SEO Audit tab showed SEO score 78 with Common errors (0), Other errors (6, among them a missing favicon and an article length message) and Good (14).
claims.plan: Free level only; no plan screen came up and the paid app SEO & Speed was not opened
claims.comparability: The in-app score against the draft that was read by hand; no outside SEO tool was used and the score was not compared with another app.
claims.buying_consequence: The number is the app's own score; the draft had no featured image and its headings repeat the search phrase, so a good score does not tell you the article reads well.

claims.observed: The draft says 152-156 cm for a 160 pound rider, a stance of +15 front and -5 back and US men's size 9 and under. We saw no invented brands, prices or product names, but these figures came with no source and were not checked.
claims.plan: Free level only; no plan screen came up and the paid app SEO & Speed was not opened
claims.comparability: The figures in the draft against a source that the draft does not give; no manufacturer chart was consulted.
claims.buying_consequence: You should check size and stance figures in a generated guide before publishing it, because the app names no source for them.

claims.claim: Insert a product into the post

claims.buying_consequence: A draft needs product links and a picture added by you before it can sell anything; how well the insert works is not confirmed.

claims.claim: Paid plans include shared AI credits, so you can write more posts and auto-fix SEO issues as you go.

claims.plan: Free level only; no plan screen came up and the paid app SEO & Speed was not opened
claims.comparability: The banner text against a plan page that was never opened; the other app and its prices were not looked at.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Tapita AEO/GEO AI Blog (the app calls itself Tapita GEO & AI Blog) on a Shopify development store: the install without a payment screen on the free level, one draft article for beginner snowboard buyers written in about 45 seconds and 6 clicks plus typing (summary block, three comparison tables, an FAQ with FAQPage schema, in-app SEO score 78), the 55 credit balance, the counter Published posts 0 / 1 and a banner that points to the paid app SEO & Speed. The draft was left as a hidden draft and nothing was published. It had no store product links and no featured image, and it held some figures with no source. Name: the App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/tapita-ai-seo-blog-builder) is now titled Tapita AEO/GEO AI Blog, listed earlier as Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder (the dossier name). Developer Tapita, Built for Shopify, Pricing Free, rating 4.9 from 493 reviews on the listing today (494 in our test on 17 Nov 2026), read at about 23:11. In the Shopify admin the app is called Tapita GEO & AI Blog and its welcome page says Welcome to Tapita AI Blog Builder: the same product under three names. The review should say Tapita AEO/GEO AI Blog, formerly Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder. Install: the install form was sent in our own tab at about 23:12 and Install app was clicked. The app asks to View staff and contributor data (store owner, blog contributors) and to View and edit store data (Products, Online Store). No payment screen came up, no separate Tapita account, password or Google login was needed: the app opened straight in the Shopify admin on the free level. Onboarding: the app started a nine step analysis of the store on its own. A pop-up Business Information asked for a Business Description and a Target Customer, which were filled with a short test text about snowboards. An Ideas Suggestions list (55 credits, 2 posts, scheduled for 11/18 to 11/25) offered Generate Blog Posts Now and Bulk Generate (2 posts); neither was used because it would schedule posts. A banner warned that the app should be opened regularly to keep processes active because of expiring Shopify access tokens. Core action: Content Studio, Create content, Blog / Informational, Create with AI opened the form Create blog post, marked 55 AI credits: language English (US), writing style, voice tone and complexity on Default, Include Summary Block on, Auto-apply FAQPage schema on, our own keyword (how to choose a snowboard for beginners), the post title How to Choose a Snowboard as a Beginner, a publish date of 17 Nov 2026, a reminder to refresh after 30 days and Generate featured image off. It took 6 clicks plus typing. Generate was clicked at about 23:13; the app showed four progress steps (Article Outline & Structure, SEO Metadata & Search Intent, Section Content Writing, Layout, Accordion & Featured Image) and said Article generated successfully! after about 45 seconds (about 23:14). The post was a Draft with Visibility Hidden. The dashboard then said Published posts 0 / 1, 1 posts scheduled and GEO health score 100%. Nothing was published and Publish was not clicked. Shopify, Content, Blog posts stayed empty: the draft lives inside the app. What the draft contained: a summary block at the top, H2 and H3 headings, three comparison tables (board type, rider profile, new, used or rental), bullet and numbered lists and an FAQ accordion titled What Beginners Should Know Before Choosing a Snowboard, with the FAQPage schema switched on (the generated code on a published page was not inspected). The advice read as generally sound and careful (Treat the chart as the starting point; weight and size chart instead of the chin height rule; flex roughly 3-5 on a 10-point scale). We saw no invented brands, prices or product names. We did see specific figures with no source, for example 152-156 cm for a 160 pound rider, a stance of +15 front and -5 back and US men's size 9 and under; they were not checked. The draft had no links to store products because nothing was inserted with Insert a product into the post, and no featured image (the box was empty). The headings repeat the search phrase almost word for word, for example How to Choose a Snowboard for Beginners: Start With Your Riding Goals, some are long and contain a dash, and the draft has many headings and tables but little voice of its own. SEO audit in the app: SEO score 78, Common errors (0), Other errors (6, among them a missing favicon and an article length message) and Good (14); a GEO tab is next to it. The button for a visibility date was marked as a locked feature, which suggests a paid function; no price was seen. Plans and limits: no Shopify approval screen and no plan list came up; the app started on the free level, labelled Free, with the line GEO Studio, free. In our test (17 Nov 2026) the dashboard showed Published posts 0 / 1, which suggests a limit of one published post on the free level, but no text confirmed it and nothing was published. In our test (17 Nov 2026) the create form showed a balance of 55 AI credits and we did not read what this draft cost in credits. A banner offered 50% off the first 3 months of SEO & Speed, a different and paid app, and said GEO Studio is free but its AI writing runs on credits from SEO & Speed; paid plans include shared AI credits. That banner was not clicked and SEO & Speed was not installed. Difference with the dossier: the dossier says Free per the Shopify listing, with no credit allowance published. In our test (17 Nov 2026) the app showed a credit balance (55), a visible 0 / 1 published posts counter and a banner that pointed to the paid app SEO & Speed for more writing. No price field is changed here. Cancelling: no paid plan was started, so there was nothing to cancel. Uninstall is in the app menu (a menu with Uninstall as its last item) or under Settings, Apps; the dialog Uninstall Tapita GEO & AI Blog? says data managed by the app will be deleted and that a request is sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information. Not tested: publishing, scheduling, Bulk Generate, Content Ideas and campaigns, the Keywords tab, generating a featured image, inserting a product or collection, translations, Preview, SEO & Speed, AI citation tracking (0 on a new store) and the quality of the published HTML. Clean up: the draft stayed in the app and nothing was added to Shopify Blog posts; no theme was changed. Tapita GEO & AI Blog was uninstalled through Settings, Apps with the reason Testing multiple apps, and Shopify said it was successfully uninstalled at about 23:17. Other apps were not touched and our own tab was closed. The price fields are not changed here. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The draft had no links to store products until we add them and no featured image. The headings repeat the search phrase almost word for word and the text has little voice of its own. Some figures (a board length for a 160 pound rider, a stance angle) came with no source. The dossier mentions no credit allowance, but in our test (17 Nov 2026) the app showed 55 credits, a counter of 0 / 1 published posts and a banner that sent you to the paid app SEO & Speed for more writing. The name also changed: the listing, the admin and the welcome page use three different names.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

not_tested: Original store creation and identity check, which we did ourselves.
Publishing, scheduling and Bulk Generate.
Inserting a product or collection, generating a featured image and the Preview.
Content Ideas, the Keywords tab, translations and AI citation tracking.
SEO & Speed and any paid plan, and what the draft cost in credits.
Export and reimport.

Session and source-reading date: 17 November 2026. Times are CET. The session started at about 23:12 CET. These are approximate tester observations, not benchmark timings. Midnight timestamps are required date anchors, not measured event times.

claim_checks.comparability: The listing price against a Shopify approval screen that never appeared; no tax, term or stored cost rule was compared.
